spec_table.original: Final architecture: a recipe line, once accepted, stayed for good: nothing re-checked the old (pre-shift) tasks until a new shift raised a score alarm, and nothing removed a line that had stopped earning its keep
spec_table.ours: **Recipe expiry, replay and pruning** (`amoeba/adapt/retention.py`: `retention_due`, `retention_check`, `retention_alarm`, `remove_line`, `prune_family`; `amoeba/adapt/gate.py::decide_prune`; `amoeba/adapt/experimenter.py::replay` (recipe A against any recipe B; `experiment` now calls it), `changes_draft`; `amoeba/adapt/loop.py::_retention`; adapt.yaml `retention: {every: 12, prune: end}`, diagnoser `allowed_edits.retention`; `scripts/run_loop.py` `--retention-every N` (0 off), `--prune end\|off`; `scripts/prune_recipe.py`). *Retention replay*: every N practice tasks of a family (default 12) the family's pre-shift gate tasks (held-out phase `pre`) are replayed with the current recipe and with the seed (v1), same seeds, through the arm-A cache; a drop larger than the family's calibration noise raises an alarm of kind/cause `retention` at once (not at the next shift). It goes through the normal Diagnoser → Architect → Experimenter → Gate path with its own ids (`o<order>r-h<n>`), allowed edits remove_planner_rule / add_planner_rule / tighten_done_when / add_role_rule; the Diagnoser gets the scores only (held-out tasks never reach a prompt); no rollback watch follows it. Each replay is a `retention` row in `retention.jsonl` and events.jsonl (resumable by its event key). *Pruning*: at the end of a stream (default) and on demand, each line of the current recipe (rule, transform, run option, model preference) is removed one at a time (`remove_line`, version + 1, `created_by: prune`) and replayed against the recipe with it on the gate set (post and pre slices; same draft unless the line changes what Box 1/2 read). `decide_prune`: remove it when the score does not fall by more than the noise AND the cost falls (USD when both arms have prices, else tokens). Each prune is a ledger `decision` row with `prune: true`, the line and its provenance, and a `prune` event; an accepted prune is committed like any accept. Prune rows count toward no hypothesis quota, no Bonferroni N and are never shown to the Architect as failed hypotheses; summary.json lists them under `prunes`
spec_table.why: an accepted edit is not forever: what hurts the old tasks raises an alarm early, and what no longer helps is taken out by the same Gate

spec_table.original: Final architecture: a task's family (which picks its recipe, D82/D88) came only from the task source; a free-text task was always `freeform`, so it never started from what the loop had learned for its kind of task
spec_table.ours: **Task family for new tasks (warm start)** (`amoeba/task/interpret.py`: `load_families`, `family_by_rule`, `classify_family`; `amoeba/config/families.yaml`; prompt `amoeba/config/prompts/family_classify.txt` (ours); `scripts/run_task.py` `run_one(family_classify, recipe_source)`, `family_classify_on`, `--family-classify auto\|on\|off`; `RunResult.family`; the mock knows the `family_classifier` kind). Box 1 gives a task whose source named no family (`freeform`) a family: first the keyword rules of families.yaml (case-insensitive whole words; the family with the most matches wins, a tie decides nothing); only when no rule decides, one routed call (router role `family_classifier`, D97) choosing from the family list or "new"; code checks the answer against the list (anything else → "new", `llm_invalid`). A known family starts from that family's current recipe in `--recipes`, else `--recipes-from` (D88); "new" starts empty (a Phase 1 run). result.json `family` records the family, how it was chosen (`rule` + the matched keywords, `llm`, `llm_invalid`) and the recipe version it started from; a `task_family` trace event too. A task whose source named its family is untouched. `auto` (default) = on for the plan runner, off for the baselines. Shipped families: calc, research, document, code
spec_table.why: a free-text task starts from what the loop already learned for its kind of task, and the choice is a rule anyone can read, with the model asked only when no rule fits

spec_table.original: Final architecture: the environment a task runs in (which tools and models are allowed, the sandbox limits, the domain's rules and words, what "done" means, extra domain checks, safety limits) was spread over CLI flags and configs, and nothing let a plan or a prompt know it, or stopped a plan from using a tool the environment should not have
spec_table.ours: **Niche profiles** (`profiles/<niche>.yaml`: `general` (today's behaviour exactly) and `calc`; `amoeba/config/niche.py`: `NicheProfile`, `load_profile`, `tool_allowed`, `environment_text`, `add_done_clauses`; `amoeba/checks/` (plug-in interface `check(output, evidence) -> (pass, reason)`, `run_checks`; `amoeba/checks/calc.py`); `amoeba/interp/runtime.py::_tool` (the refusal guard); `amoeba/interp/plan_runner.py` `PlanOptions.domain_checks`, `domain_checks`; `amoeba/task/interpret.py::read_task(environment)`; `amoeba/localtools/toolbox.py::LocalSetup.with_limits`; `scripts/run_task.py` `--niche` (default general), `niche_tools`, `run_one(niche)`, the router's `profile_allowed` and verifier setting). One file per environment: allowed tools (names or patterns) and the D96 sandbox limits (timeout per command, CPU, memory, time per run — A2: per profile), allowed models and the verifier-independence setting (feeding the D97 router), domain rules and vocabulary, default done clauses, domain checks to run, safety limits (USD, tokens, calls per run; outside actions). Prompts stay generic: one "Environment" section ("Assess this environment first: which tools you have, what is limited, what counts as done; plan only with what is allowed." + the profile's facts) is appended to Box 1's interpretation prompt and to Box 2's Planner and both Observers' prompts. Enforcement is code: Box 2 is shown only the allowed tools; Box 3 refuses any tool outside the profile (or, with `outside_actions: false`, any tool with an outside-action word) even if a plan or replan gives it to a role, logs a `niche_refused` trace event and runs nothing; the router refuses any model outside the profile (D97 filter `profile`); the profile's done clauses are added by code to the answer step; its domain checks run after each step next to the step checks (`source: domain`), and a failed one earns the same retry turn. `calc` check: every figure in the answer must be a number the task states or a calc / local-tool result of the run (at its written precision); counts 0–10, bare years and step numbers are not figures. `general` is neutral (every tool, every model, no Environment section, no check, no limit): prompts, plans and results are byte-identical to a run without `--niche` (tested). Plan runner only; the baselines never get a profile
spec_table.why: one readable file says what an environment allows and expects; the team is told once, and code holds it to it

spec_table.original: Probe (hard) problem 9: a session restart moved the HTTPS proxy, and runs started before it ended with `api: APIConnectionError`; such a run counted as a finished run with score 0 (four M-P2 check runs had to be moved aside by hand), and the Gate's reliability rule counted it as the team's error
spec_table.ours: **Infrastructure errors are a status, not a score** (`amoeba/task/models.py::run_status`, `infra_error`; `RunResult.status`; `amoeba/adapt/experimenter.py` `infra_cfg`, `RunRecord.crashed`/`status`, `_scored_pairs`, `ReplayResult.excluded`, both runners; `amoeba/adapt/gate.py::honesty_shares`; `amoeba/adapt/monitor.py` `PracticeRecord.status`; `amoeba/adapt/loop.py`; `amoeba/adapt/retention.py::_mean_score`; `amoeba/config/proxy.py`; `amoeba/llm/client.py`; adapt.yaml `infra: {retries: 2, exclude: true}`). Every result.json records `status`: `ok`, `agent_error`, or `infra_error` — an `api:` error after the client's own retries (connection, timeout, proxy, 429, 5xx, auth; a 400/413/422 is what the team sent and stays `agent_error`), a `cache_miss`, or a runner that left no result. The Experimenter's runners and the loop's practice runs run an infra-error run again, at most 2 times; a (task, k) whose arm is still infra after that is left out of the pairs and listed in `experiment.json` `excluded`; a practice run still infra is recorded with `status: infra_error`, score None, an `infra_error` evidence event, and the Monitor never sees it; Gate rule 5b counts agent errors only. Proxy: `AMOEBA_PROXY_FILE` names a file that always holds the current proxy (`HTTPS_PROXY=<url>`, or the first loopback proxy URL in it); on a dropped connection the client reads it and, when the proxy moved, sets it in its environment and rebuilds its HTTP client before the next try; the harness refreshes the environment it hands each run the same way. Unset, nothing changes
spec_table.why: a lost connection costs a retry, never a score, and a moved proxy no longer breaks running processes

spec_table.original: Probe (hard) problem 7: in H3 the verifier's own blind answer differed from the worker on the BEV price and the electricity rate, yet its verdict was PASS with "Issues: none"; plain code recorded the difference (D90 `own_only`) but nothing acted on it. Amended after a review of VeriHarness: the disagreement is settled by a separate resolver against the evidence, not by a rework of the worker
spec_table.ours: **The disagreement resolver** (`amoeba/interp/disputes.py`: `labelled_figures`, `disputed_figures`, `agree`, `disputes_text`, `parse_resolution`, `settle`, `replace_figure`; `amoeba/config/prompts/plan_resolve.txt`; `amoeba/interp/plan_runner.py` `PlanOptions.disputes`, `run_step`, `resolve_disputes`, `enforce_limitations`; `scripts/run_task.py --disputes on|off`, default on). With `--verify-first on`, plain code pairs each figure of the verifier's blind result with the checked outputs' figures by label (the words before the number on its line; at least two shared words, or the shorter label ends the longer; same kind: $, % or plain; bare years and counts ≤ 10 left out) and compares the values with the rubric's tolerance (5% relative, or equal at the coarser precision written). A labelled figure the outputs state only with a different value is a disagreement (`disputed` event). All of a step's disagreements go to one separate, fresh call — the verify step's first helper with `plan_resolve.txt`, which sees only the disputed figures, both lines and the source text the team was shown — whose only job is to settle each one by the source text, a fetch, a calculation or a re-run in the sandbox, writing per figure `Value`, `Evidence` (a quote copied from the source, or the command and its output line) and `Verdict`. Plain code disposes: a figure counts as settled only when its quote is in a source text and states the value, or the value is in the resolver's own tool output; it then records `worker` (the worker's value stands), `verifier` or `corrected`; anything else is `unresolved`. A settled value that differs from the worker's replaces it in the producer's output (later steps and the answer see it; the producer's `resolved_figures` record it). An unresolved figure keeps the step from PASS: the step is partial ("disputed, unresolved"), a PASS is recorded as `verdict: DISPUTED` with `verdict_model: PASS`, and plain code adds "DISPUTED: <label> — step k gives A; the check in step n, worked out independently, gives B" to the answer's Limitations. `step_N.json` keeps `dispute` {state resolved/unresolved, figures, resolutions}; every resolution is a `dispute_resolution` event (value, evidence, kind, verdict, replaced). A figure the outputs never state stays in D90's `own_only`. Off, nothing changes
spec_table.why: a disagreement between two independent answers is settled by evidence or shown, never dropped

spec_table.original: Probe (hard) problem 3: H2 ended with `error: null` while every committed output (CSV, PNG, adjusted values) was BLOCKED; nothing in result.json said the team delivered nothing, and the re-plan's requirement status trusted the steps' claims. Amended after a review of ScholarEvolve: D105 and D110 are one final-answer requirement check
spec_table.ours: **The final-answer requirement check, part 1: requirements and files** (`amoeba/task/deliverables.py`: `requirement_terms`, `requirement_check`, `final_check`, `final_findings`, `no_deliverable_of`, `promised_files`, `answer_content`, `check_deliverables`; `amoeba/interp/plan_runner.py` `PlanOptions.final_check`, `final_answer_check`, `run_step` (answer step), `enforce_limitations`, `requirement_status`; `amoeba/task/models.py` `Episode.final_check`, `RunResult.deliverables`, `RunResult.requirement_status`, `run_status`; `scripts/run_task.py` `run_one(deliverable_check)`, `--deliverable-check on|off`, default on, plan only). After the summariser writes the answer, plain code checks the FINAL answer: each requirement of Box 2's list (D24/D35) is met when the answer holds at least half of its key terms (content words of four letters or more, by their first five letters, and its numbers) and no BLOCKED line of the answer is about it (two key terms or more); a requirement that asks for a file is met only when the file exists; and every file the plan promised (named in a step output or a requirement, or asked for by kind: CSV, workbook, chart image, Word document, PDF, slide deck) must be in the workspace (by name, else by kind; with `--local-tools on`). Together with D110's dates, the missing items are findings of the answer step's one refine turn. What is still missing after it goes into Limitations ("NOT MET: R2 — … (checked by plain code on the final answer)", "MISSING FILE: …"), and the run ends `error: "no_deliverable: …"`, `status: no_deliverable` when a core deliverable is missing: no answer content (80 characters without headings, BLOCKED lines and Limitations), a promised file never made, or more than half of the requirements unmet. result.json records `deliverables` (the whole check) and `requirement_status` (each requirement as checked on the final answer); with `--replan on` the re-plan's requirement status takes the final-answer result and keeps the steps' claim as `steps_claim`. The baselines are never checked
spec_table.why: a run that did not deliver says so, judged on what the user receives

spec_table.original: Probe (hard) problem 1: in sandbox mode every pool skill was refused as "not in the sandbox image" (xlsx in H1, docx in H3), because `attach_skill` resolved the entry's `root` — a label such as `anthropics_skills` — against the current directory as if it were a path; and the live test for this fix found a second blocker: the Bash gate refused any command naming `/opt/skills`, so a helper could read a skill but never run its scripts
spec_table.ours: **Pool skills work in sandbox mode** (`amoeba/localtools/skills.py`: entries keep `root_path`; `skill_root_path` (an older entry finds the label among its path's parents), `sandbox_skill_path`; `amoeba/localtools/toolbox.py::attach_skill`; `amoeba/localtools/gate.py::screen_command(readonly)`). A skill of the baked-in clone maps to `/opt/skills/<its path in the clone>` (the image copies `data/pool/repos/anthropics_skills` there); a skill of any other root is still refused and logged. In the sandbox a Bash command may name paths under the config's `readable_roots` (`/opt/skills`) — a helper runs a skill's scripts from there — while writing there is refused by `protected_command` first and fails in the sandbox anyway (read-only, root-owned). In-process mode is unchanged. Tests: offline mapping and attach in sandbox mode; live (skipped without the gateway and image): the xlsx skill is attached to a helper in a fresh sandbox, its SKILL.md read with local:Read, its scripts listed and parsed with local:Bash
spec_table.why: the skills the pool picks reach the helpers in the sandbox

spec_table.original: Probe (hard) problem 4: in H2 and H3 single queries packed every entity, year and series together ("US Indiana median household income 2015 2016 … 2023 CPI-U", even several quoted queries in one string), very few pages were read (2 fetches in 14 searches in H2; one California article twice in H3), and H2's data sat in linked .xlsx tables that a page view never reaches
spec_table.ours: **Research steps: split queries, read the top primary sources, parse linked data files** (`amoeba/tools/research.py`: `split_query`, `official`, `rank_official`, `excerpt`, `data_links`, `data_ext`, `parse_table`, `table_excerpt`; `amoeba/tools/web.py`: `http_get`, `TavilyProvider.fetch_data`/`page_links`, `WebLimits` research limits, `WebTools.research`, `_search_one`, `_read_top`, `_linked_data`, `_read_data`; `amoeba/llm/cache.py` `CachedProvider.fetch_data`/`page_links` (cached like search and fetch); `amoeba/interp/plan_runner.py` `RESEARCH_NOTE`; `scripts/run_task.py --research on|off`, default on, plan runner with `--web-tools` only). Plain code splits a packed web_search into at most 4 searches: several quoted queries in one string become one each; several places (US states, countries, the US by any of its names, "and"/commas between them dropped) one per place; several years one per year when that stays within 4, else one year range per search. Each search ranks official domains first (.gov/.mil/.edu/.int and statistical agencies) and plain code reads its top 3 results itself (a page already read in the run counts), showing the lines that match the query (700 characters each); a read page's data-file links (.csv/.tsv/.xlsx/.xlsm/.json, in its text or, failing that, its HTML) are fetched directly (best match to the query first, 2 per page) and parsed into a table (CSV/TSV, the first sheet of a workbook, a JSON list of records), shown as the header rows plus the rows naming a query word, each with its own [S#]; a fetch_url of a data file reads it as a table. Limits per step: 9 such reads, 4 data files. The step note tells helpers to search one entity, year or series at a time and to prefer the official source and the data file. Off (and for the baselines) nothing changes
spec_table.why: a research step reads the primary data instead of guessing from snippets

spec_table.original: Probe (hard) problem 5: the sandbox has no network by design, so the figures a researcher fetched reached the analyst only as prose; no code could compute from them (H2's analyst and chart roles made zero sandbox calls)
spec_table.ours: **Fetched data in the workspace, read-only** (`amoeba/localtools/toolbox.py`: `INPUTS`, `LocalToolbox.add_input`, `save_source`, `inputs`, `_snapshot` leaves sources/ out; `amoeba/localtools/sandbox.py::OpenShellBox.pull` (sources/ not copied back); `amoeba/localtools/gate.py` (`sources` protected: writes refused, reading and copying from it allowed); `amoeba/tools/web.py` `WebTools.on_data`, `_page` (every fetched page, also by fetch_url); `amoeba/interp/plan_runner.py` `SOURCES_NOTE`; `scripts/run_task.py` `run_one(workspace_sources)`, `--workspace-sources on|off`, default on, plan runner with web and local tools). Every page and data file the web tools read is written by the harness to `<workspace>/sources/` — data tables as `S<n>_<name>.csv`, pages as `S<n>_<title>.txt` (with its source id, url and title on top) — on the host and, in sandbox mode, into the sandbox's workspace (uploaded through the sandbox API, `chmod 0444`); `sources/index.json` lists each file with its [S#], url, title, kind, rows, fetch time and step (its provenance), and the web source record gets `workspace_file`; a page's text counts as seen for the D74 citation check. Inputs are never counted as files the team made. A step whose helpers have local tools is told which files are there and to cite a figure from a file by its [S#]. The sandbox keeps no network
spec_table.why: analysts compute from the fetched data itself

spec_table.original: Probe (hard) problem 6: both of H2's re-plans added steps with the same role, tools and query style as the failed step, and they failed the same way; the Action Observer (D63) was never shown how the failed step had worked, and nothing checked a re-plan against it
spec_table.ours: **A re-plan must change the method that failed** (`amoeba/interp/replan_method.py`: `failed_method`, `replaces`, `method_change`, `failed_methods_text`; `amoeba/interp/plan_runner.py` `PlanOptions.replan_method`, `failed_steps`, `same_method`, `validate_decision`, `_observer_call`; `scripts/run_task.py --replan-method on|off`, default on, with `--replan on`). A finished step failed when it is partial or incomplete, lacked a capability, or is a verify step still failing or disputed. The observer is shown, for each, the tools it used (or its roles held), the sites and source types it read (official, data) and its queries, and is told that a step for it must change the method and say how. Plain code then checks every step the decision adds or rewrites: one that replaces a failed step (it covers the same requirements, or the same role does nearly the same thing: word overlap ≥ 0.4) must state at least one change in its text — a tool the failed step never used (named in the step), a source type it never read (a data file or table, an official source, an API), a site it never read, or a decomposed query (one search per entity, year or series). A step that states none makes the whole decision rejected, with "step N repeats the method of failed step M (tools …; sources …)" in the validation errors; every check is logged (`replan_method` event: which step it replaces, the changes found, the failed method). Off, nothing changes
spec_table.why: a re-plan tries something different instead of failing the same way twice

spec_table.original: Probe (hard) problem 8: H3 asked to cite every figure with its date, and no figure in the memo had one; nothing checked dates on figures. Amended: part of D105's final-answer requirement check
spec_table.ours: **The final-answer requirement check, part 2: dates on web figures** (`amoeba/interp/dates.py`: `undated_figures`, `dated_finding`; `amoeba/task/deliverables.py` `final_check`, `final_findings`; `amoeba/interp/plan_runner.py` `PlanOptions.dated`, `final_answer_check`, `enforce_limitations`; `scripts/run_task.py --dated-figures on|off`, default on). In the same check as D105, on the final answer, plain code finds every figure (years left out) on a line that cites a web source ([S#] of a search or fetched page); it carries a date when its line states one (a year, month and year, a quarter, an ISO date, "as of", a fiscal year) or when every source it cites has a dated entry under the answer's Sources/References heading. Undated figures are findings of the answer step's one refine turn, shared with D105's; figures still undated after it are listed by plain code in Limitations ("- UNDATED: $250,000 [S1] — the source's date (publication or data period) is not stated") and logged (`undated_figures`; `final_check` event). Figures in the Limitations section, computed figures without a web citation and local-tool results are not checked. Off, nothing changes
spec_table.why: a reader can tell how old each web figure is, or is told it is not stated

spec_table.original: Probe (hard) problem 2: the D74 citation check flagged arithmetic as mislabelled citations — a result computed on the line from cited inputs ("350 + 1,428.00 = 1,778.00 [S3]"), a power ("4¹⁰ = 1,048,576"), the years of a range beside a source ("2016 … 2019 [S5]") — and each flag alone set a step to partial (H1 ended partial with a correct answer)
spec_table.ours: **The citation check skips in-line arithmetic** (`amoeba/interp/citecheck.py`: `RESULT`, `POWER`, `YEAR_RANGE`, `derived_tokens`, `claims(arithmetic)`, `mislabelled_citations(arithmetic)`; `amoeba/interp/plan_runner.py` `PlanOptions.cite_arithmetic`; `scripts/run_task.py --cite-arithmetic on|off`, default on). In the words an [S#] backs, a number the line shows as a calculation's result (after `=` or `≈`, with `~` or a currency sign allowed), the base and exponent of a power (`4¹⁰`, `4^10`) and the two years of a range (`2016–2019`, `2016 … 2019`, `2016 to 2019`) are not claims of their own; the calculation's operands and every other number are still checked against the source. Off, the check is as before
spec_table.why: a correct calculation no longer turns a step partial

spec_table.original: Probe (hard) problem 10: the H1 verifier's first call sent a fenced Python block to local:Bash, which failed with a shell syntax error (it recovered on the next turn, one turn lost)
spec_table.ours: **Python sent to local:Bash runs with python3** (`amoeba/localtools/toolbox.py`: `python_source`, `as_python_command`, `PY_FENCE`, `PY_START`, `LocalToolbox.arguments`; `amoeba/config/localtools.yaml` `bash_python: true`). A local:Bash input that is a fenced block tagged `python`/`python3`/`py`, or whose first line starts like Python (`import …`, `from … import`, `def …(`, `class …`, `print(`, `with open(`, a `for … in …:` loop, a python shebang), is run as `python3 - <<'AMOEBA_PY' … AMOEBA_PY` — a quoted heredoc, so the shell expands nothing inside; the delimiter changes if the program contains it. The rewrite is logged (`bash_python` event with the line count), and the gate screens the whole command as before (a network import is still refused). Shell commands, `python3 file.py` and fenced bash blocks are untouched. `bash_python: false` turns it off
spec_table.why: a helper's Python runs instead of costing a turn

spec_table.original: Probe (hard) problem 11: in H1's workbook the per-truck weights and miles were typed in, not derived from the load table, so the workbook would not follow a change in the inputs; nothing checked a spreadsheet's formulas
spec_table.ours: **Spreadsheet checks: totals and derived cells must be formulas** (`amoeba/checks/xlsx_formulas.py`: `typed_derived_cells`, `check`; `amoeba/interp/plan_runner.py` `PlanOptions.xlsx_formulas`, `xlsx_checks`; `scripts/run_task.py --xlsx-formulas on|off`, default on, plan runner with local tools). After a step that made an .xlsx/.xlsm file, plain code opens each workbook with its formulas and lists the typed numbers that should have been formulas: a number in a total row or column (its row label or column header — text, not a formula — says total, sum, subtotal, grand total, average, mean or net), a number equal to the sum of the two or more typed numbers just left of it in its row or just above it in its column, or a number equal to the product of two of the numbers to its left. A number the task states is an input and never flagged. Any such cell fails the check `domain_xlsx_formulas` with the cell names (at most 20) and earns the step's retry turn, like a failed format check; the check is also available to niche profiles by name. An unreadable workbook fails the check with its name. Off, and without local tools, nothing is checked
spec_table.why: a delivered workbook recomputes when its inputs change

spec_table.original: Review of two papers (VeriHarness, ScholarEvolve): the loop could tune the team's rules, transforms, run options and model preferences, but not how much context a step and the summariser are shown (fixed CLI values, 6,000 and 30,000 characters), although lost context is a common failure
spec_table.ours: **Context size as recipe run options** (`amoeba/config/adapt.yaml` `recipe.run_options.max_input_chars {min: 3000, max: 20000}`, `max_summary_input_chars {min: 15000, max: 60000}`; `diagnoser.allowed_edits` `checks: + set_run_option:max_input_chars`, `feedback: + set_run_option:max_input_chars, set_run_option:max_summary_input_chars`; `amoeba/adapt/recipe.py::PLAN_OPTION_NAMES`, `overlay_run_options`, V2 in `validate_recipe`; `scripts/run_task.py` `OPTION_FLAGS`, `INT_OPTIONS`). A recipe may set either option with `set_run_option` inside its range (outside: V2); the value overlays the plan runner's `PlanOptions` like the other run options (a CLI flag given explicitly still wins, D82) and is recorded in result.json's `recipe.run_options` and the `plan_graph` event; `--option-defaults` accepts them as integers. The Architect may propose them only for the checks and feedback causes, and the Gate tests them like any edit. Defaults unchanged
spec_table.why: the loop can tune context size, through the Gate

spec_table.original: User request (Oct 6): when the interpretation step would assume a reading (no reading leads the next by 0.3, a tie included), always ask the user first instead of guessing; D77 asked only with --interactive and only about the least certain entity
spec_table.ours: **Ask on every assumed reading** (`--ask-assumed on`, the CLI default). Before Box 2, every entity whose reading would be assumed is asked about, least certain first, one multiple-choice question each (its readings + other), through --interactive's prompt or else the terminal (`ask_all`, `scripts/run_task.py::can_ask`). The answer is settled `user` and the task note says so. A blank reply keeps that one assumption, stated as in D77. With nobody to ask (no terminal) the run stops before Box 2 with error `needs_clarification` (status `needs_clarification`), writes `clarification.json` (each entity, its options, its lead) and records the questions in result.json (`interpretation.pending`); `--clarify ENTITY=READING` (repeatable; words or an option number) answers ahead of time and settles those entities with no question (`apply_clarify`). `--ask-assumed off` keeps D77. The experiment harness passes off (`adapt.yaml experiment.run_flags`): no one answers in an experiment, loop or audit run, and a paused M-P2 resumes unchanged. Tests: tests/test_ask_assumed_d116.py
spec_table.why: the user, not a guess, settles what the task is about

spec_table.original: User decision (Oct 6): drop the offline learning loop; adaptation happens inside a single task, when a Box 3 step gets stuck, from that run's own logs, results and errors; nothing carries over between tasks
spec_table.ours: **Stage A, the removal.** Deleted: task streams (`amoeba/adapt/stream.py`, `tasks/stream_*`, `tasks/audit/`), the Experimenter, the Gate and its statistics, calibration, the ledger, the Monitor, the loop's Diagnoser, the Architect's prompt and proposal loop and its human queue, the recipe store (`amoeba/memory/recipes.py`, `--recipes`, `--recipes-from`, the recipe hook in Boxes 2–3), retention replays, pruning, user-memory proposals and approvals, the loop driver, and `scripts/run_loop.py`, `run_experiment.py`, `run_audit.py`, `prune_recipe.py`, `approve_memory.py`. Kept: the step contract's causes (they become stuck signals), the cause → allowed-edit table (`adapt.yaml diagnoser`), the single-edit JSON format and its checks (`amoeba/adapt/architect.py`: `ArchitectReply`, `parse_reply`, `check(reply, allowed, recipe, failed)`), the edit menu, transforms and V1–V6 (`amoeba/adapt/recipe.py`), and the hash-chained event log with the evidence branch (`amoeba/adapt/evidence.py`). The family classifier (D101) only records the family. Stages B–E: stuck watch and diagnosis (code), code fixes, a fix-proposer agent, `--adapt on|off`. Tests: tests/test_edit_format_d117.py; loop tests removed, mixed ones trimmed. **Stage B, the stuck watch (code only, no fix).** `amoeba/adapt/stuck.py`: five signals (repeated_error → new cause tool_error, checks_after_retry → checks, max_turns, capability_unfilled → capability, no_file_change → claimed_file_missing); a step that did not end done with a signal is STUCK; one cause by the table order. `PlanRunner.watch` after each attempt with `--adapt on` (CLI default; library default off) → `meta["stuck"]`, trace `stuck`, `<run>/events.jsonl`, `result.json` `stuck`. `scripts/stuck_report.py` counts stored runs. Tests: tests/test_stuck_d117.py. **Stage C, code fixes (no AI).** New cause missing_input (data an earlier step should have given; fixed before capability). `amoeba/adapt/fixes.py` lists the fixes cheapest first: add the dependency / pass the artifact; re-run the upstream step once with the item in its done_when (the only redo of a completed step); more turns; more retry turns; a larger input; attach the missing tool from the pool shortlist (code pick; skipped with "capability fix unavailable: pool off"). `PlanRunner.fix_stuck` re-runs only the stuck step; limits in adapt.yaml `adapt` (3 per step, 8 per task, token and dollar caps, never a repeat); none recovers it → the task stops with `adapt_report.md`, status `stuck`. boxes.title: 4 · Adapt within the task
boxes.sentence: D117: the offline learning loop is gone; adaptation happens inside one task, when a Box 3 step gets stuck.
what: Stage B (built): after each step attempt plain code looks for the stuck signals, marks the step STUCK, diagnoses one cause and logs it.
Stage C (built): code fixes, cheapest first — pass a missing input or re-run its upstream step once, more turns or retry turns or a larger input, attach the missing tool from the pool shortlist.

Stage D (built): when the code fixes are used up or not allowed, the fix proposer (one AI call) proposes one edit; plain code checks and applies it. Within limits; when nothing recovers the step the task stops with a report.
Kept for the fixes: the cause → edit table, the single-edit format with V1–V6, and the hash-chained event log.
Nothing carries over between tasks.

boxes.title: Planner
boxes.sentence: An AI writes the list of helpers and a numbered step plan; later rounds see only the latest critique.
what: The planning AI reads the job and the tools that exist, then writes each helper as a small record and a numbered plan saying which helper does which step.
From the second round on it also sees its own last draft and the checkers' latest suggestions.
Its reply must contain five labelled parts; see Split sections for what happens if one is missing.
It is told to prefer the tools that exist; a tool or skill it needs but we lack goes in an optional sixth part, Capability Requests, which costs no retry when absent.
At most three rounds are run.

With our prompts (d24) it may also list Open Questions: each ambiguity in the job and the assumption it took. With --interactive the person sees the requirements, assumptions and open questions and types continue, or a correction that is added to the job before one more round.

D68: with our prompts it and both checkers are shown every tool the team will really have (calc, web search and fetch, the local tools and skills when on, and that a tool pool exists); a document format or a house style is a skill; what only the user can supply is an open question or a request; tools that are disabled are hidden from this list.

boxes.disposes: Nothing is accepted yet: the draft goes to the two checkers, and only the last draft is cleaned and checked by plain code after the loop.

It is told to prefer the tools that exist; a tool or skill it needs but we lack goes in an optional sixth part, Capability Requests, which costs no retry when absent.
At most three rounds are run.

With our prompts (d24) it may also list Open Questions: each ambiguity in the job and the assumption it took. With --interactive the person sees the requirements, assumptions and open questions and types continue, or a correction that is added to the job before one more round.

D68: with our prompts it and both checkers are shown every tool the team will really have (calc, web search and fetch, the local tools and skills when on, and that a tool pool exists); a document format or a house style is a skill; what only the user can supply is an open question or a request; tools that are disabled are hidden from this list.

boxes.title: Task interpretation and family (D77, D101)
boxes.sentence: Before the Planner drafts, an AI lists what the task's names and terms could mean; plain code takes a clear winner, asks the user one question, or makes the answer state its assumption.
what: One call reads the task (and the read-only user context from --context: location, organisation, role) and lists the key entities and terms that could be read more than one way — names, abbreviations, acronyms, likely voice-input errors such as "P and W" for "PNW" — each reading with a one-line reason and a confidence.

Plain code: a reading whose confidence beats the next by 0.3 or more (DOMINANCE_GAP) (or the only one) is the working interpretation. Otherwise, with --interactive, the user gets one multiple-choice question (the readings + other); without it the top reading is an assumption.

The working interpretation is added to the task text, so the Planner, both checkers and every helper in all three runners read it; an open question the Planner writes about one of these names is answered from it, not by its guess.
After the run, when the reading was assumed, plain code makes the answer open with "I read X as Y; if you meant Z, …" and lists the other readings under Limitations, adding whatever is missing.

D116: with --ask-assumed on (the CLI default) every reading that would be assumed, a tie included, is asked about before planning, one question each, least certain first; with nobody to ask the run stops with needs_clarification and writes clarification.json, and --clarify ENTITY=READING answers ahead of time; off keeps the behaviour above, and experiment runs pass off.
boxes.proposes: The entities, their readings, a reason and a confidence for each.
boxes.disposes: Plain code decides whether a reading is clear, whether to ask, and checks the answer's opening line.

boxes.plan: Plain-code checks on the final draft
boxes.sentence: Throws out broken or nameless helper entries, records tools we lack instead of dropping them, flags the summariser, and drops steps that name nobody.
what: Reads the helper records and the numbered steps out of the last draft.
Skips records that are not valid, have no name, or repeat a name; tools we lack go to the tool resolver below.
Flags the summariser: the helper the planner marked, else the last helper of the last step (having no tools no longer decides it; nothing is appended). Then requires a team size in the allowed range.
Matches each step's names to helpers (exact first, then by part of the name) and drops steps that match nobody; no steps left means drafting failed.

Measures the draft: every requirement covered, dependencies valid, helpers fully described, one summariser, a checking step done by a helper that did not produce what it checks, and task coverage: every number in the task and every deliverable verb (deliver, estimate, assess, prototype, test, gather, build, plan, and since D68 run, convert, email, make, save, write, list, read, compute, compare and more) must reach a requirement or a given; a phrase ends at sentence punctuation, not inside an email address or a decimal.
With the quality gate on by default, a draft failing a must-have check goes back to the planner for one more round with the failed checks listed, within the round cap.

With --web-tools, a role that asked for web search, lacks specific tools, or is performing research gets web_search and fetch_url; if the task is time-sensitive, it is notified to use fresh information; if local files are available, it is provided with a summary of those files and their source identifiers.

After the step, what plain code found goes back to the helper for one refine turn (--self-refine). In a step with several roles, the first drafts and the others AGREE or REVISE with numbered issues, at most {PlanOptions.collab_rounds} rounds (--collab critique); if verification is enabled, the verifier may perform its own check, including resolving disputed figures, checking final findings, and marking missing inputs, before the final output is kept.

With --step-contract on (D61) its prompt lists what plain code will check: each capability it asked for and lacks, and each tool or skill it was given; it must use each one or write BLOCKED or NOT NEEDED with a reason.

boxes.title: Check the step
boxes.sentence: Checks each step's output against its output and done-when lines and, with the step contract, what its helpers lacked and used; reads verdicts and gaps.
what: Checks what the planner said the step produces: the table:, list:, code: or memo: markers in its output line (keywords only when there are none), and a real use of its inputs.
A failed check gets one retry with the reasons and two turns of its own; otherwise the step is incomplete.

A step the planner marked kind: verify must answer PASS or FAIL; a FAIL sends each step it checked back once, then it checks again. Steps that already used the old output are marked stale (--rerun-stale redoes them once).
BLOCKED lines make a producer step partial, with the missing capability listed; the answer step is never scanned for them.

Step contract (D61, --step-contract on): before the step, plain code lists each helper's unfilled requests and the items attached to it; after it, every tool call is on record (who, which tool, ok). A lacked capability with no BLOCKED or NOT NEEDED line, or an attached item never used successfully, earns one refine turn and then makes the step partial (not declared / attached unused).
A verify step also sees each checked step's sources, tool calls, figure counts and files (D61). A producer whose only problem is a missing capability is not sent back (rework_skipped).

D65: a verify step also gets the tools to re-check (calc, web search and fetch, local run and read, through the same sandbox gate) and the raw tool results of every step it builds on; a PASS with no re-checking tool call on code, files or cited figures is an unverified check and makes it partial.

D90 blind-first verifier: with --verify-first on (the CLI default), a verify step first works out its own answer from the checked steps' inputs and its tools, in a fresh context without their outputs (plan_verify_own.txt); only then does it see the outputs, and plain code lists every figure where its own answer and the checked output differ (compare_figures). Both are kept in step_<n>.json.

D102: the niche profile's domain checks (amoeba/checks/<name>.py, e.g. calc: every final figure is a stated input or a calc result) run here next to the step checks; a failed one earns the same retry turn.

D109 (resolver): plain code pairs the verifier's blind figures with the worker's by label (5% tolerance); one fresh resolver call settles each disagreement by source text or a re-run, plain code checks its evidence, a settled value replaces the wrong one, and an unresolved one keeps the step from PASS and goes into Limitations.

D110 (part of D105's final-answer check): every web-sourced figure of the final answer must carry its source's date (line or source entry); undated ones share the refine turn, and those still undated are listed in Limitations.
D104: the citation check leaves out a calculation's result shown on the line (after = or ≈), a power's base and exponent, and the years of a range; the operands are still checked.
boxes.proposes: The step's output and verdict (from the helper); BLOCKED and NOT NEEDED lines.
boxes.disposes: Plain code decides done, partial or incomplete, the retry and the rework, from the contract and the evidence.

boxes.sentence_tpl: Checks each step's output against its output and done-when lines and, with the step contract, what its helpers lacked and used; reads verdicts and gaps.
what_tpl: Checks what the planner said the step produces: the table:, list:, code: or memo: markers in its output line (keywords only when there are none), and a real use of its inputs.
A failed check gets one retry with the reasons and two turns of its own; otherwise the step is incomplete.

A step the planner marked kind: verify must answer PASS or FAIL; a FAIL sends each step it checked back once, then it checks again. Steps that already used the old output are marked stale (--rerun-stale redoes them once).
BLOCKED lines make a producer step partial, with the missing capability listed; the answer step is never scanned for them.

Step contract (D61, --step-contract on): before the step, plain code lists each helper's unfilled requests and the items attached to it; after it, every tool call is on record (who, which tool, ok). A lacked capability with no BLOCKED or NOT NEEDED line, or an attached item never used successfully, earns one refine turn and then makes the step partial (not declared / attached unused).
A verify step also sees each checked step's sources, tool calls, figure counts and files (D61). A producer whose only problem is a missing capability is not sent back (rework_skipped).

D65: a verify step also gets the tools to re-check (calc, web search and fetch, local run and read, through the same sandbox gate) and the raw tool results of every step it builds on; a PASS with no re-checking tool call on code, files or cited figures is an unverified check and makes it partial.

D90 blind-first verifier: with --verify-first on (the CLI default), a verify step first works out its own answer from the checked steps' inputs and its tools, in a fresh context without their outputs (plan_verify_own.txt); only then does it see the outputs, and plain code lists every figure where its own answer and the checked output differ (compare_figures). Both are kept in step_<n>.json.

D102: the niche profile's domain checks (amoeba/checks/<name>.py, e.g. calc: every final figure is a stated input or a calc result) run here next to the step checks; a failed one earns the same retry turn.

D109 (resolver): plain code pairs the verifier's blind figures with the worker's by label (5% tolerance); one fresh resolver call settles each disagreement by source text or a re-run, plain code checks its evidence, a settled value replaces the wrong one, and an unresolved one keeps the step from PASS and goes into Limitations.

D110 (part of D105's final-answer check): every web-sourced figure of the final answer must carry its source's date (line or source entry); undated ones share the refine turn, and those still undated are listed in Limitations.
D104: the citation check leaves out a calculation's result shown on the line (after = or ≈), a power's base and exponent, and the years of a range; the operands are still checked.

boxes.title: Action Observer (re-plan)
boxes.sentence: With --replan on, after a wave where something went wrong or changed, an AI may re-plan the steps that have not run; plain code validates the change.
what: Plain code looks for a trigger after each wave: a step that lacked a capability, a verify step still failing, a step reporting a missing input, or a tool the plan did not know about. No trigger, no call.

One planner call sees the task, the plan with each step's status, what the finished steps produced, what is blocked, the tools really available and the budget left, and returns one decision: CONTINUE, REVISE_REMAINING, ADD_STEP, REASSIGN_STEP, DROP_STEP or ADD_ROLE. Each requirement is marked as met if its covering step is done and no check fails; ADD_ROLE triggers the creation of a new helper with its assigned tools.

Code rejects any change to a finished step, unknown roles or tools, an incomplete new role card, a team too large, a loop, or a new step that depends on a step that has not run. New capability requests go through the normal toolbox step; a dropped requirement is listed as not met, and finished steps are tracked by their claim status.
At most 2 re-plans and 3 added steps per run; an unreadable or invalid reply counts as CONTINUE. Each accepted plan is saved as plan.v2.json, plan.v3.json … with the change.

D108: a step a re-plan adds or rewrites for a failed step must state a different tool, source type, site or a split query, else the decision is rejected and logged; the observer is shown each failed step's tools, sources and queries.
boxes.proposes: One typed decision and its reason.
boxes.disposes: Plain code decides when to call, validates the decision, applies it and records every version.

boxes.title: Summariser assembles
boxes.sentence: An AI assembles the final answer from every step's output, adding nothing new, and lists the gaps.
what: Sees every step's latest output with its status, missing capabilities, verdict, figure counts, the deliverables the plan committed to, and where each figure was found (never the scoring rubric).
Must add no new analysis or numbers, answer in the form the job asks for, and list gaps under Limitations when there are any.
Code counts any number it adds, lists the answer's untagged and unverified figures, appends a line for any missing capability it left out, and logs these actions.

D61: it is told which files each step made. Files and source-cited figures the answer leaves out earn one refine turn; files still unnamed are listed by code, and Limitations also name undeclared missing capabilities, attached items left unused, and audit logs.

Each input is shortened to 6,000 characters and all of them to 30,000; since D64 the head, the tail and every line with a result (a count, a total, an '=' line, the last lines of program output) are kept, with a mark for what was left out. When several final steps have no summariser step, code puts their outputs together under headings, filtering out lines that repeat section headers, and logs the assembly.

D67: for a task that asks for today's, the current or the latest value, a figure whose as-of date is more than 3 days old adds 'possibly not the latest' to Limitations; it also notes where the figure was found.
boxes.disposes: Plain code counts new numbers, checks the answer against the work produced, and completes the Limitations section.

boxes.sentence: Writes one log line per AI call and tool call: who, which model, tokens, reasoning tokens, time, step, and automated safety checks. Nothing enforces a budget.
what: Every AI call becomes one log line with the helper, model, tokens in and out, reasoning tokens, time taken, and step number.
Tool calls, each helper's turn, and the whole run get their own lines too.
Point events are logged too: capability_request, blocked and unknown_tool.
From the command line each AI line also holds the exact prompt sent and the reply received (turn off with --no-log-content).
Token counts are only recorded; no code reads them to stop a run.
Every line names the model profile; each AI line holds the model asked for and the exact model name the service returned.
boxes.disposes: Plain code writes the log.

boxes.title: RunResult
boxes.sentence: The one-line summary of a run: answer, score, calls, tokens, draft rounds and whether the checkers agreed.
what: Summarises the run in one record saved as result.json.
Calls and tokens are totalled from the log; draft rounds and agreement come from the draft.
It also lists the steps that answered BLOCKED and every capability request, and counts how many requests round 1 made and how many the checkers talked the planner out of.

D105 + D110: after the summariser, plain code checks each Box 2 requirement and each promised file against the final answer and the workspace (and the dates of web figures); missing → one refine turn, then Limitations, and no_deliverable when a core deliverable is missing; requirement_status records the final-answer result.

D116: status needs_clarification when the run stopped before planning to ask the user about a reading it would otherwise have assumed; result.json then lists the open questions (interpretation.pending).

boxes.title: Tool box
boxes.sentence: Repeat a text back or do arithmetic safely; with --web-tools the plan runner also has web search and page reading.
what: Tools are looked up by name; a name that is not registered is an error, not a web search.
The arithmetic tool accepts numbers and + − × ÷ and powers only, never arbitrary code.
web_search and fetch_url (Tavily) give every result a source id [S#]; searches and fetches per step, page length and time are capped, and a failure comes back as an error line, never a crash.
Pool tools (D56) are remote MCP servers registered as pool:<name> for the helper that asked; they run here too, with the same caps, [S#] source ids and error lines.
This is the single place any tool is ever run.

D106 (research on, plan runner): a packed web_search is split (quoted queries, places, years; at most 4); each search reads its top 3 results itself, official domains first, and parses the .csv/.xlsx/.json files a read page links into tables with their own [S#].

boxes.title: Stock the toolbox
boxes.sentence: Before the team starts, tries to fill each tool or skill the team asked for from the pool; one AI pick per request, everything else plain code.
what: Match: the cached pool entries, tools and skills alike (the requested kind is only the planner's guess; the kind asked and the kind picked are logged), are ranked by the words they share with the request (its standard name and aliases, name, what it does, input and output); the best 5 (pool.yaml) are kept. None above zero: unfilled, no AI call.

Vet first (D60): the candidates are checked before the pick and the AI is shown only the best 5 that pass (up to 50 matches are checked); if none pass, the request is unfilled (all_refused) with no AI call.

Pick: one short AI call shows the request and those candidates and must answer exactly one listed id or NONE; any other reply counts as NONE. It gets 6,000 tokens of room, and once more with twice that when the reply is cut off.

Vet: a tool must be read-only (nothing in its name or description that sends, posts, pays or deletes, or creates, updates, uploads, edits or writes anything in an outside service, D60) and not a pay-per-call host; it needs an HTTPS remote, a source repository, a pinned version, no key or its key in the environment, and an unchanged description (also re-checked against the server's tools/list at every connection); a skill must be instruction-only and at most 5,000 characters. At most 3 items per helper and 8 per run (pool.yaml).
Attach: a tool becomes pool:<name> for the asking helper only; a skill's text goes on that helper's card. All pool text is shown inside marked data blocks, and the 'unavailable' line goes away.
Every request's outcome and reason code is written to capability_requests.json and result.json; without a pool cache the run logs pool_unavailable and goes on as before.

With --local-tools on (D59) the local toolbox's items are candidates too — ahead of the pool's only when an alias names them or they match at least as well (D61) — and a skill with scripts is no longer refused: it is copied into the run's workspace.
What became of each request (filled or not) is handed to the plan runner for the step contract (D61).
D69: a request that names a document format (xlsx, docx, pptx, pdf) gets the vetted local skill for it, chosen by plain code with no AI pick; an outside service that creates things stays refused.
D70: with --picks-file every run of a task reuses the task's first pick for a request (all three architectures), when it passes vetting again; --picks-only makes the picks in a pre-pass.
boxes.proposes: The picker names one candidate (or NONE).
boxes.disposes: Plain code ranks the candidates, rejects anything unsafe or over the caps, and attaches.

boxes.sentence_tpl: Before the team starts, tries to fill each tool or skill the team asked for from the pool; one AI pick per request, everything else plain code.
what_tpl: Match: the cached pool entries, tools and skills alike (the requested kind is only the planner's guess; the kind asked and the kind picked are logged), are ranked by the words they share with the request (its standard name and aliases, name, what it does, input and output); the best {rank.top} (pool.yaml) are kept. None above zero: unfilled, no AI call.

Vet first (D60): the candidates are checked before the pick and the AI is shown only the best {rank.top} that pass (up to 50 matches are checked); if none pass, the request is unfilled (all_refused) with no AI call.

Pick: one short AI call shows the request and those candidates and must answer exactly one listed id or NONE; any other reply counts as NONE. It gets {PoolLimits.max_result_chars} tokens of room, and once more with twice that when the reply is cut off.

Vet: a tool must be read-only (nothing in its name or description that sends, posts, pays or deletes, or creates, updates, uploads, edits or writes anything in an outside service, D60) and not a pay-per-call host; it needs an HTTPS remote, a source repository, a pinned version, no key or its key in the environment, and an unchanged description (also re-checked against the server's tools/list at every connection); a skill must be instruction-only and at most 5,000 characters. At most {PoolLimits.max_calls_per_step} items per helper and 8 per run (pool.yaml).
Attach: a tool becomes pool:<name> for the asking helper only; a skill's text goes on that helper's card. All pool text is shown inside marked data blocks, and the 'unavailable' line goes away.
Every request's outcome and reason code is written to capability_requests.json and result.json; without a pool cache the run logs pool_unavailable and goes on as before.

With --local-tools on (D59) the local toolbox's items are candidates too — ahead of the pool's only when an alias names them or they match at least as well (D61) — and a skill with scripts is no longer refused: it is copied into the run's workspace.
What became of each request (filled or not) is handed to the plan runner for the step contract (D61).
D69: a request that names a document format (xlsx, docx, pptx, pdf) gets the vetted local skill for it, chosen by plain code with no AI pick; an outside service that creates things stays refused.
D70: with --picks-file every run of a task reuses the task's first pick for a request (all three architectures), when it passes vetting again; --picks-only makes the picks in a pre-pass.
boxes.text_stale: the model's reply was unusable or wrote a number the code does not hold

boxes.title: Local toolbox (OpenShell sandbox, D96)
boxes.sentence: With --local-tools on, Claude Code's tools and skills run in a fresh OpenShell sandbox per run: no network, only the workspace writable.
what: D96: `claude mcp serve` and every command run inside a fresh OpenShell sandbox per run (image amoeba-sandbox:local, gateway on 127.0.0.1:17680): no network, Landlock lets only /sandbox, /tmp and /dev/null be written, skills are read-only under /opt/skills, no secrets, runs as user sandbox; the sandbox is deleted at the end.

The harness gate refuses first what it can see: network commands, paths outside the workspace, writes to MCP configs, hooks, settings, CLAUDE.md or skills (protected_config); what a command hides is stopped by the sandbox. Files are copied back to runs/<id>/workspace/ after each call.
Limits: 300 s per command (D96a), 1 CPU, 1 GiB, one hour per run, 8,000 characters of output, 20 calls per step and 60 per run; a niche profile can set its own sandbox limits (D102).

--local-tools-mode sandbox is the default; inprocess (the earlier host process) runs only when asked for and needs AMOEBA_SANDBOX=1. Every allow and deny decision goes to the trace and from there to events.jsonl (tool_decisions); a live test shows the agent cannot reach the OpenShell gateway API.

Skills are listed only from the kept anthropics/skills clone; an attached skill's SKILL.md goes on the helper's card. Aliases (code runner → local:Bash, spreadsheet → the xlsx skill …) put local items first (D61).

D103: in the sandbox a pool skill maps to /opt/skills/<name> (the entry's root is a label; its folder is root_path), and Bash may name /opt/skills read-only so the skill's scripts run; writing there is refused.

D107: every page and data file the web tools read is saved read-only under sources/ in the workspace (and uploaded into the sandbox), with sources/index.json giving each file's [S#], url and time; writes there are refused and the files never count as made.
D112: a Python program sent to local:Bash (a ```python block, or a first line that starts like Python) runs as python3 from a quoted heredoc; the rewrite is logged and the gate still screens it.
boxes.proposes: A helper's tool call (name and input); the picker's choice of a local item.
boxes.disposes: Plain code allows the tool, checks every path and command, caps calls and output, and checks claimed files.

Skills: SKILL.md files from a shallow git clone of github.com/anthropics/skills (only the repository named in pool.yaml), with whether the skill ships scripts and the length of its text; the skill folders are kept whole under repos/ for the local toolbox (D59).

boxes.title: AI connection
boxes.sentence: The connection to any AI service that speaks the OpenAI format; it reports what each reply cost in tokens.
what: Sends the messages to the AI service and returns the reply with its token counts.

Waits out rate limits (HTTP 429/503: up to five retries, Retry-After honoured, each wait logged), dropped connections and timeouts too; an error still there after that ends the run with error 'api: …' and its records are still written. boxes.title: Edit menu, transforms and V1–V6 (kept from D81)
boxes.sentence: The typed edits a fix may make, the code that applies them to a plan, and the plain-code validation every edit must pass.
what: The edit menu: add or remove a planner rule, add a check step after selected steps, add a clause to selected steps' done-when, grant or revoke a tool on selected roles, add a rule to selected roles' cards, set one run option, prefer a model (built, off). Each edit is a pure function that makes version N+1 with parent N.
Transforms apply an edit to a Draft: add a verify step, tighten done_when, grant or revoke a tool, add a role rule; each returns what it changed.

Validation by plain code (V1–V6): tools are in the registry and not outside actions; run options are whitelisted and in range (max_turns 3–8, check_retry_turns 1–3, input sizes); at most 8 rules and 8 transforms of at most 300 characters (amoeba/config/adapt.yaml); no wording that tells the team to skip checks, citations or the sandbox; the step graph still passes the plan checks; a model preference names a known role and model.
D117: there is no recipe store and no recipe hook any more; nothing carries over between tasks. A Recipe is only the container one task's edits are checked in.
boxes.disposes: Plain code applies an edit, applies the transforms and refuses one that breaks V1–V6.

boxes.title: Event log and evidence branch (kept from D95)
boxes.sentence: An append-only, hash-chained log written only by the harness, with a fingerprint of every run folder it names, and an off-container copy on the repository's evidence branch.

D117: the loop that wrote it is gone; the log is kept for in-task adaptation, where every stuck step, diagnosis and fix will be a row.

boxes.title: Model router (D97–D98)
boxes.sentence: Picks the model for every LLM call by plain-code rules: allowed and available models, hard filters that are never relaxed, then a preference set for the role (D98, built, off), the role's default or the cheapest of the right size.
what: Every call states its role, step, size, needed features and data class; the router keeps the models that are allowed (niche profile, --allowed-models) and available (key present, not cooling down, not failing), drops those whose context, features, privacy, budget or verifier-independence rule fails, then chooses.
One token bucket per model, shared by every process, keeps calls inside the model's per-minute limits; a 429 cools a model down and the next one of the same size is used (with one model: wait).
Every decision — candidates, what was filtered and why, the choice, fallbacks and waits — is logged; result.json gets calls, tokens and US dollars per model. A new model is a registry entry only.

D98: a prefer_model edit (built, off) fills the router's per-role preference; it is used only when that model is still a candidate after every filter, and a verifier preference for the checked work's family is logged as verifier_same_family: recipe preference.
D102: the niche profile's model allowlist and verifier-independence setting feed the router; a model outside the profile is filtered out with reason profile.
boxes.proposes: Nothing: no AI takes part in the decision.
boxes.disposes: Plain code picks the model; no call is made when no model passes the filters (no_model).

boxes.title: Stuck watch and diagnosis (D117 Stage B)
boxes.sentence: After each step attempt plain code marks a step that did not end done STUCK on any of six signals and names one cause.
what: Signals: a missing input (data an earlier step should have given, told from a missing tool by classify_lacked); the same tool error twice in a row (digits masked); checks still failing after the retry turn (unless the helpers ran out of turns); max turns; a capability or skill lacked or requested and unfilled; a file owed and no file change between attempts.
Each signal names a cause; the first cause in the table order wins, with its allowed edits and at most eight evidence lines.
The event goes to the trace, step_N.json, result.json (stuck) and the run's hash-chained events.jsonl. --adapt on is the command-line default.

boxes.sentence: The last rung: one AI call proposes one edit for the stuck step; plain code checks it, applies it to the live plan and re-runs the step.
what: Called only when the code fixes for the step are used up or not allowed (including "capability fix unavailable: pool off").

It sees the task, the step's card and done_when, the cause and evidence, the last attempt's errors and checks (trimmed), the team (one line per role), the tools and skills of this run, the edits the cause allows and the fixes already tried.

It returns one JSON edit with a short reason: add_role_rule, add_helper_role (the Planner's role card), grant_tool (tools of this run only), split_step (two or three sub-steps), replan_remaining (the Planner's plan format, for the part not done) or work_around (capability only, after a grant_tool or add_helper_role was tried for the step; stated under Limitations; counted as finished with limitation, never recovered). At most two added helpers per task.

Plain code checks: allowed for the cause, schema, V1 tools, V3 sizes, V4 wording, V5 team size and step graph, done steps untouched, not a repeat; one retry on an invalid reply, a second failure is no fix. The adaptation limits apply; success is the step ending done.
boxes.proposes: One edit with a reason (fix_proposer prompt).
boxes.disposes: Plain code refuses, or applies the edit and judges the step by its checks and contract.

boxes.title: Stage E: --adapt off vs on (pairs and report)
boxes.sentence: Runs each task and seed with --adapt off, then on with the off run's draft and pool picks, and reports the two arms side by side.
what: The on arm reuses the off run's plan.json (--drafts-from) and both share one --picks-file: the arms differ only in Box 3. A pair whose arm already has a result is not run again.

The report: outcome per run (done, done with limitation, stuck-stopped, failed), stuck steps by cause (the off arm read offline by the same watch), recovered steps by rung, work-arounds apart, rubric scores, billed tokens, the adaptation's tokens and $, wall time, searches, and what broke.
Three recovered steps per arm, picked at random with a fixed seed, are shown with their trace lines and their output before and after.
boxes.disposes: Plain code runs the pairs and counts.

boxes.title: Single-edit format and check (kept from D87)
boxes.sentence: One proposed change is one strict JSON object; plain code parses it and checks it is allowed, valid and new.
what: The reply: exactly one JSON object with one typed edit, a short rationale (at most 400 characters) and a predicted change between -1 and 1; any other key is refused.
Plain code checks that the edit is allowed for the cause (adapt.yaml), that the edited recipe passes V1–V6, and that the same edit was not already tried.

glossary: helper
One AI worker in a team, with its own name, instructions and allowed tools.
team shape (topology)
How helpers are connected; fixed when a run starts, never chosen by an AI.
step by step (flat)
The plan's steps run in order; each step's helpers take turns until they give a final answer.
one writer with reviewers (boss + reviewers)
One helper writes the answer, the others review it, the writer revises on objections.
draft
The planner's proposed helpers and step plan for one round.
round
One planner reply plus one reply from each checker.
turn
One reply from each helper of a step.
consensus
Both checkers wrote 'No Suggestions' in the same round.
section
A '## Heading' part of an AI reply that plain code cuts out and reads.
guard
A plain-code check that rejects, corrects or caps what an AI produced (shield icon).
envelope
The fixed rules a team must satisfy: allowed tools per role and the team-size limit.
trace
The log file with one line per AI call, tool call, helper turn and run.
token
The unit AI services count text in; recorded per call, never enforced in Phase 1.
sample run
One practice job run with the offline stand-in AI when this page was built.
stand-in AI
A scripted fake AI used offline; it is not a real model.
deviation
A deliberate difference from the original AutoAgents / AgentVerse code, marked in the source.

gaps.title: Capability record → step status
gaps.missing: Which requests each helper asked for and did not get (capability_requests.json, missing_tools) never reaches the status check: a step is 'done' unless the helper itself wrote BLOCKED.
evidence: r1-route, all rounds: distances from memory in a 'done' step with no routing tool
r1-code-run, round 2b: 'done' without the code being run
gaps.direction: A step whose helper has an unfilled request cannot be 'done' without saying what it did instead.
gaps.fix: D61: before the step plain code lists each helper's unfilled requests (step contract, shown on its prompt); after it, one that is neither BLOCKED nor NOT NEEDED earns one refine turn, then makes the step partial ("not declared by the helper").

gaps.title: Tool-call trace → step status
gaps.missing: Whether the helper called the tool or skill attached for its request is logged (execute_tool, local_call) but never read when the step is judged.
evidence: r1-deck, round 2: pool slide tool attached, 0 calls, step 'done'
r1-deck, round 3: pptx skill + local tools attached, 0 calls, step 'done'
gaps.direction: An attached item that was never called is recorded on the step, and the helper must say why.
gaps.fix: D61: every tool call of the step is recorded (who, tool, ok); an attached item with no successful call and no BLOCKED / NOT NEEDED line earns one refine turn, then makes the step partial ("attached unused").

gaps.title: Capability record → Limitations
gaps.missing: Limitations are built only from the BLOCKED marks helpers wrote; the run's unfilled requests are never compared with the answer.
evidence: r1-fx-email, all 4 rounds: the missing email sender is never named
r1-route: the missing routing tool is never named; r1-weather 2b: missing current conditions not named
gaps.direction: Every unfilled capability request appears in Limitations, whatever the helpers wrote.
gaps.fix: D61: Limitations also get every undeclared missing capability and every attached item left unused (NOT USED lines), matched by canonical name.

gaps.title: Checked step's sources → verifier
gaps.missing: A verify step sees only its declared inputs, not the tool results behind the step it checks.
evidence: r1-weather, round 2: a real, cited forecast fetched in step 1; the verifier (depends on step 2 only) wrote BLOCKED 'Step 1 output' and the answer said 'failed verification'
gaps.direction: A verifier also receives the sources of the steps it checks.
gaps.fix: D61: a verify step's inputs carry, per checked step, its sources, tool calls (ok or failed), figure counts, files made and what it lacked or left unused.

gaps.title: Produced work → answer check
gaps.missing: Figures and files produced upstream (figure ledger, files_created) are recorded but never checked against the final answer; after a FAIL the summariser writes a status memo instead.
evidence: r1-xlsx, rounds 1–2b: lane totals, 79,800 and 1,855.81 computed in step 1, absent from every answer
gaps.direction: The answer carries every usable result produced upstream, next to what is missing.
gaps.fix: D61: the answer step is told which files each step made; files and source-cited figures the answer leaves out earn one refine turn, and files still unnamed are listed by plain code.

gaps.title: Failure cause → rework
gaps.missing: On a FAIL verdict every checked producer is re-run, whatever the cause; a missing capability does not change between attempts.
evidence: rework in 6 of 10 runs in round 2 and again in 2b; none changed a blocked step (r1-full-chain: 3 reworks, 2 stale)
gaps.direction: Skip rework when the producer's only problem is a capability it does not have.
gaps.fix: D61: each step records its causes; a producer whose only cause is a missing capability is not reworked (rework_skipped).

gaps.title: Local tool result → source list
gaps.missing: A local tool's output gets no source id, so provenance cannot count a figure taken from it as cited.
evidence: r1-code-run, round 3: the executed F50 = 12586269025 cited as '[S1]', counted as a made-up citation
gaps.direction: Give each local result a source id ('local run'), shared with the run's [S#] list.
gaps.fix: D61: a successful local call gets an [S#] in the run's one source list (kind local), and the step's sources include it.
